messages:
meera: FYI I'm doing judge onboarding for the new q4-judgemodel (4-bit) — CI for the eval-harness keeps flaking on judge runs. seeing disagreement spikes vs the r2 judge.
jay: ugh saw that too. reproducción steps point to a race in the runner: when we cancel and reschedule batches the judge micro-batch sometimes gets a stale kv-cache flag. i'll open a PR for a quick fix.
alex: can we also agree on a deterministic tie-breaker/rubric? right now ties are 'first-come' which makes A/B noisy. propose: 1) if judges disagree, pick the output with higher mean confidence; 2) if confidences within 0.08, mark as INCONCLUSIVE and queue for human sample; 3) if both judges low confidence (<0.35), auto-fail.
sophia: agree on INCONCLUSIVE bucket. also we should add paraphrase consistency check (run 3 paraphrases and expect >=80% same label) — catches brittle judge prompts.
meera: +1. also worth adding a calibration metric (ECE) and a "flip rate" metric (how often judge changes label on re-run). For the quantized judge, small calibration shifts are expected; we need threshold baselines from the original float judge.
jay: eval-bot reproduced the failure and left logs:
```
[eval-runner] ERROR 2026-03-21 15:44:10 - judge_worker.py:142 - kv_cache flag mismatch on batch_id=1732
Traceback: ... IndexError on offsets
```
I'll patch the runner to zero the kv flag on retry; should cut flakiness.
alex: For CI wiring: add a new integration gate that runs 200 random eval samples with both judges (r2 and q4) and reports: agreement_rate, mean_confidence_delta, ECE_delta. Block if agreement_rate drops > 3% or mean_confidence_delta > 0.12.
sophia: also surface these on the infra dashboard. Panels: judge_agreement_over_time, judge_flip_rate, judge_ece_by_bucket, per-class disagreement heatmap, and per-prompt-length breakdown.
meera: quick rubric snippet we can include in the harness config (proposal):
```
"rubric": {
  "labels": ["A","B","C","INCONCLUSIVE"],
  "tie_break": ["mean_confidence","median_confidence","human_fallback"],
  "confidence_thresholds": {"low":0.35, "inconclusive_margin":0.08},
  "paraphrase_consistency_k":3,
  "paraphrase_threshold":0.8
}
```
jay: that looks clean. small ask: make sure the harness records per-judge raw logits so we can recompute calibration after quantization experiments.
meera: yes, we will store logits and seed. also add a hash of model binary + quantization config to the run metadata so dashboards can filter by quantization variant.
eval-bot: CI: eval-harness-integration (pr #4281) — 1 failing test (judge_integration.test_agreement_threshold) — rerun recommended.
ci-bot: re-run queued (attempt 2 of 3)
alex: while the runner fix lands, we should add unit tests to replicate the race. sample pytest assertion:
```
def test_kv_flag_reset_on_retry(runner):
    runner.simulate_cancel_then_retry(batch_id=42)
    assert not runner.batches[42].kv_flag, "kv_flag should be reset after retry"
```
This will catch regressions instead of flaky integration failures.
sophia: good. For dashboards I'll add alerting: when judge_agreement drops by >2.5% vs baseline in last 24h -> send to #eng-ml and page on major customers. also create a daily report with a small sample of INCONCLUSIVE items for review.
meera: plan summary:
- jay patches runner race + unit test (today)
- alex adds CI integration gate + agreement/block thresholds (tomorrow)
- sophia wires dashboard panels and alerting (this week)
- meera will run baseline quantized-vs-float comparison and publish calibration + flip-rate numbers (by Friday)
- if INCONCLUSIVE > 1% on production evals, enable human sampling and escalate
any objections?
jay: none from me. going to send PR shortly.
alex: no objections. can you @me when baseline numbers are in?
meera: will do. thanks! :rocket:
